page: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-48 is a graphics-optimized GPU instance designed for compute-intensive visualization, simulation, and machine learning workloads. Powered by an x86_64 CPU architecture, the server allocates 48 dedicated vCPUs paired with 180 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU core. It incorporates a single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 accelerator from the Blackwell GPU family, providing 96 GB of dedicated VRAM. The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached block storage for all operational and persistence layers.

The presence of 96 GB VRAM on a single accelerator enables execution of large neural network inference models, photorealistic ray tracing, and complex CAD or visual effects rendering tasks without requiring multi-GPU synchronization overhead. System host memory is proportional to the processor count, accommodating large datasets before paging. Because local storage is absent, throughput to persistent disks depends on network bandwidth configuration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g4-standard-48 offers balanced resource density by pairing an enterprise workstation-class GPU with an expansive 48-vCPU host platform. This architecture minimizes hypervisor contention through dedicated core pinning. It suits production workloads including high-fidelity 3D graphics rendering, virtual workstation streaming, computer vision processing, and deep learning model inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-48 is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance tailored for advanced graphical rendering, simulation, and machine learning workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it provides 48 dedicated vCPUs alongside 180 GB of system memory, matching roughly 3.75 GB of RAM per core. The hardware configuration features a single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPU from the Blackwell family, offering 96 GB of dedicated video memory for heavy visual computing and large-scale model inference. The instance contains no bundled local storage, requiring network-based volumes for operational data. Providing dedicated compute cores and substantial VRAM, the g4-standard-48 functions effectively for visual effects rendering pipelines, CAD workstations, spatial data processing, and enterprise artificial intelligence inference tasks.
